thread.title: Berkshire Hathaway's Warren Buffett To Buy Stake In India's Paytm

author: APARNA NARAYANAN
title: Berkshire Hathaway's Warren Buffett To Buy Stake In India's Paytm
text:
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway ( BRKB ) has taken a small but significant stake in India's largest digital payments platform Paytm. Buffett's hefty financial investments already include Visa ( V ), Mastercard ( MA ) and American Express ( AXP ), which are themselves transforming to seize explosive growth in mobile payments.
X Berkshire Hathaway confirmed an investment in Paytm parent One97 Communications in an email to Reuters, but didn't offer any details. Sources told Reuters that Berkshire would take a 3%-4% stake, valuing One97 at more than $10 billion.
India's Economic Times on Monday reported Berkshire Hathaway was in talks for a 3%-4% stake, but for a slightly lower price range of $286 million to $357 million. Unidentified sources later confirmed a pact to Bloomberg, which said a formal announcement could come within days.
The Paytm deal is the billionaire investor's first direct investment in India.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Paytm is already backed by Japan's SoftBank Vision Fund as well as Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba ( BABA ) and its Ant Financial arm. B-class shares of Berkshire Hathaway rose 0.1% to close at 210.77 on the stock market today , after climbing 1.2% on Monday. They are basing above the 50-day moving average in a consolidation with a 217.72 buy point. Visa fell 0.1%, Mastercard rose 0.5%, and American Express added 0.2%. Alibaba fell 1.4% after a 3.7% jump Monday.
Berkshire Hathaway Investments Apple ( AAPL ) accounts for nearly a quarter of Berkshire's stock investment portfolio. Apple Pay is seen as a future growth driver.
Besides Visa, American Express and Mastercard, Buffett's financial holdings include U.S. Bancorp ( USB ), Bank of New York Mellon ( BK ), Synchrony Financial ( SYF ), Goldman Sachs ( GS ), Wells Fargo ( WFC ) and Bank of America ( BAC ).
Infusing financial services with technology could transform the investing landscape for India's 1.3 billion people, experts say.
